entries.reason: Own docs show a runnable curl example — 'GET /v1/models' with 'Authorization: Bearer $ABLIT_KEY' — plus a nav/API-reference structure with dedicated 'openai-chat-completions', 'openai-compatibility' and 'openai-responses' sections, and Login/Console/Get-API-key/Signup links. Pricing is stated as usage-based, billed per token, with plans and credit packs (no free tier mentioned). The unauthenticated /v1/models call correctly 401s with a structured missing_api_key error, consistent with a real gated API. Note: the vendor's whole positioning ('abliterated' models) is about deliberately refusal-removed/uncensored LLMs — worth a content-policy flag for whoever considers integrating it, independent of the technical verdict.

Own docs API-reference nav literally lists 'POST /v1/messages' and 'POST /v1/chat/completions' plus text beginning 'One OpenAI-compatibl[e]...', with 'Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-<key>' and the explicit statement that 'API keys are issued after purchase at above.dev/pricing' (no free tier). Unauthenticated GET /v1/models returned a real 9-model catalog directly in the OpenAI list shape. This is a multi-model routing gateway (also exposes an Anthropic-shaped /v1/messages route), a legitimate category NeuroLink already ships one example of (openrouter).

AI21's own API reference shows POST https://api.ai21.com/studio/v1/chat/completions taking model+messages (system/user/assistant/tool) with Bearer auth; the response reference page (docs.ai21.com/reference/jamba-api-response) confirms a top-level 'choices' array with per-choice 'index' and message content, matching the OpenAI shape (models: jamba-large, jamba-mini). Unusually, unauthenticated GET /v1/models returns HTTP 200 but an empty {"data":[]} rather than a 401/403 — the endpoint exists but lists nothing without credentials. AI21's own pricing docs state new accounts get a $10 credit valid 3 months usable across API/SDK/playground before billing info is required.

Bearer auth confirmed. Live unauthenticated GET /v1/models returned 401 with a clean OpenAI-style auth error ("missing credentials — use Authorization: Bearer <token>").
